source: order.jsonl of each round-A policy arm on the box (LTR_ORDER_LOG)
measured: 2026-07-27, after the critique that stock-calibrated arrival may leave the faster policy base without a queue
reading: The arrival rate was calibrated to 90% of the stock scheduler's saturation. The policy base drains 44% faster, so at that rate its waiting queue is empty at the 90th percentile and holds two or more requests in under 1% of scheduling steps. The ordering null and the implementation gap are one phenomenon: the faster base erased the queue that ordering would have acted on. TTLT for policy arms (mean 2.7 s against ~0.1 s service) accrues in continuous-batch decode contention, not in the waiting queue.

request_level.source: block1-main round-A order logs (LTR_ORDER_LOG), one file per arm
request_level.definition: depth of the waiting queue at each request's first appearance in it; inversion = a step whose emitted order differs from arrival order
request_level.note: PolicyFCFS records zero inversions by construction, validating the counter; step-level ge2_pct is diluted by decode ticks and understates per-request reorder opportunity.
